sections.heading: Hero
sections.body: An island climbing destination with mountain crags, volcanic-looking formations and documented routes around Roque Nublo.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.body:
Gran Canaria is best treated as an island climbing destination rather than a single crag. The known climbing sits in mountain terrain, with Roque Nublo standing out as a clear example.

The island format matters for planning: the climbing is part of a broader mountain and coastal trip, and moving between bases is more important than it would be at a compact village crag.

sections.heading: Rock and climbing character
sections.body: The supported rock evidence for this batch is basalt conglomerate at Roque Nublo. That points to varied holds and mountain-style movement rather than the clean limestone rhythm found at many mainland sport areas.

sections.heading: Grades and difficulty
sections.body: Roque Nublo is documented with 12 routes, but that does not make a reliable island-wide grade range. Use a current climbing guide or local topo for full-island grades and route choice.

sections.heading: Transport and access
sections.body: Gran Canaria is a flight-access destination. For climbing, a car is the practical choice because the relevant terrain is inland and mountainous rather than concentrated beside one resort town.

sections.heading: FAQ
sections.body:
Is Gran Canaria a single climbing area? No. Treat it as an island destination with separated mountain climbing areas.

Is this a full climbing guide? No. Use current climbing-specific information for route counts, grades and season advice before planning the fine details.
